definition.message:
{{#is_alert}}
## What's happening?

File system **{{mount.name}}** on firewall **{{device_ip.name}}** is {{value}}% full.
{{/is_alert}}

{{#is_warning}}
## What's happening?

File system **{{mount.name}}** on firewall **{{device_ip.name}}** is {{value}}% full. This monitor alerts above 97%.
{{/is_warning}}

{{#is_recovery}}
## Recovered

File system {{mount.name}} on firewall {{device_ip.name}} is back below 85% used.
{{/is_recovery}}

{{^is_recovery}}

---

## Impact

Logging, software and content updates, and commits may fail.

---

## Why?

Possible causes:
* **Old software images** left after upgrades.
* **Debug, core, or tech support files.**

---

## How to troubleshoot and resolve the issue?

1. Run `show system disk-space` on the firewall to confirm which mount is full.
2. Delete unused software images with `delete software version <version>`.
3. Delete old debug and core files.

---

## Related links

* [Documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/pan_firewall/)
* [Metrics Explorer](/metric/explorer?exp_metric=pan_firewall.disk.used_pct&exp_scope=device_ip:{{device_ip.name}},mount:{{mount.name}}&exp_agg=max&exp_type=line)
{{/is_recovery}}
definition.name: [Palo Alto Networks Firewall] File system {{mount.name}} is nearly full on {{device_ip.name}}

description: Tracks the percentage of space used on each file system of the firewall. A full file system can stop logging and block updates and commits. The log partition `/opt/panlogs` is excluded: PAN-OS fills it up to the log quota and purges the oldest logs, so high usage there is normal.
title: File system is nearly full
